content.user_title: Build MCP Servers for AI Integrations
content.value_statement: Connecting AI assistants to services requires careful server design. This skill guides planning, TypeScript structure, tool annotations, testing, and evaluation for MCP servers.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a four phase workflow for MCP server planning, implementation, review, and evaluation.
Recommends stdio, Streamable HTTP, or SSE transports for common deployment environments.
Shows a TypeScript server structure with tool registration and request handling concepts.
Explains read-only, destructive, idempotent, and open-world tool annotation categories.
Provides MCP Inspector commands for local server testing.
Defines an evaluation format for checking tool use and expected answers.
limitations: It is a guide, not a complete production MCP server.
It does not include real service authentication or authorization flows.
It does not generate full source files without additional user direction.
Example URLs and tool names must be replaced for each project.

use_cases.title: Plan a New MCP Integration
use_cases.description: Map the target API, choose a transport, and define tools before writing server code.

use_cases.title: Review Tool Safety Labels
use_cases.description: Classify each tool by read behavior, destructive impact, repeat safety, and external system effects.

use_cases.title: Create Evaluation Scenarios
use_cases.description: Write practical questions that verify tool calls, expected outputs, and read-only behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Start an MCP Server Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an MCP server for [service]. Identify tools, transport, authentication needs, and first evaluation questions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MCP tools for [workflow]. Include names, descriptions, input fields, safety annotations, and expected error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Server Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this MCP server structure for clarity, transport choice, tool boundaries, and test coverage: [project outline].

prompt_templates.title: Build Evaluation Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation for an existing server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create ten read-only MCP evaluation scenarios for [server]. Include expected tools, validation criteria, and edge cases.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a customer support API.
output_examples.output: A phased plan with service research, transport choice, tool list, safety labels, test steps, and evaluation questions.

output_examples.input: Review tool annotations for account management actions.
output: Read tools are separated from update tools.
Destructive actions require explicit names and narrow inputs.
External effects are marked for human review.

output_examples.input: Create evaluations for a reporting MCP server.
output_examples.output: A set of verification scenarios with expected tool usage, measurable answers, and read-only constraints.

best_practices: Start with the target API model, user workflows, and safety boundaries before coding tools.
Use specific tool names and actionable error messages that help the AI recover.
Test with MCP Inspector and add evaluations that reflect real user questions.
anti_patterns: Do not expose broad tools that hide many unrelated actions behind one name.
Do not mark destructive operations as read-only or idempotent.
Do not ship a server without tests for common errors and edge cases.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design and document MCP servers that connect AI assistants to external services.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready source code?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure, examples, testing guidance, and evaluation patterns for your implementation.

faq.question: Which language does the guide emphasize?
faq.answer: The guide emphasizes TypeScript and the Model Context Protocol SDK.

faq.question: Can I use it for remote MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE transport options for different environments.

faq.question: Does it cover safety annotations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains read-only, destructive, idempotent, and open-world tool categories.

faq.question: How should I verify my MCP server?
faq.answer: Use MCP Inspector for manual testing, then create evaluations with expected tools and validation rules.
